title: Minimum Edge Toggles on a Tree
summary: Given an undirected tree with n nodes, represented by a 2D integer array of edges, and two binary strings indicating the initial and desired colors of each node, determine the minimum number of edge toggles required to transform the initial colors into the desired colors.
statement: Given an undirected tree with n nodes, represented by a 2D integer array of edges, and two binary strings indicating the initial and desired colors of each node, determine the minimum number of edge toggles required to transform the initial colors into the desired colors. Return the indices of the edges to toggle in increasing order. If it is impossible to achieve the desired colors, return an array containing the single element -1.
constraints: 2≤n≤100,000 and edges is a valid indexed tree.
Toggling an edge flips both endpoint bits.
Return the minimum toggle edge indices sorted, or [-1] if impossible.
hints: Root the tree; a non-root node can be fixed from below only by deciding whether to toggle its parent edge.
Process nodes bottom-up: if a node still differs, its parent edge is forced and also flips the parent’s requirement.
After all children, the root must already match or the transformation is impossible.
Every chosen edge is forced by its child endpoint, proving uniqueness and minimum size; sorting yields the required output order.
editorial: Every chosen edge is forced by its child endpoint, proving uniqueness and minimum size; sorting yields the required output order.

tests.explanation: Only edge zero must toggle, producing the target directly.
One endpoint alone cannot be toggled by the sole edge, so return [-1].
